$comment: Registry of the interpretation decisions a from-spec AEE v0.6 verifier must make, and the corpus vectors that lock each FORCED reading. Built after the independent from-spec checker (in-toto/attestation PR #570, Rul1an) recorded eleven interpretation decisions plus four open corners. A checker agreeing with our two rails (Go aee/, Python packaging/run_vectors.py) is not proof the spec FORCES the reading; this registry classifies each decision forced|permitted, cites the vendored spec, and names the forcing vector(s). scripts/interpretation-registry-gate.py asserts every forced decision has at least one live vector present in the corpus and MANIFEST.json. Spec line refs (Lnnn) are into spec/predicates/adversarial-execution-evidence.md at the specDigest pinned in MANIFEST.json.

decisions.title: Referenced-record validity vs covers-nothing (two altitudes)
decisions.reading: The coverage-validity bullets (references resolve in range and class-match; every referenced payload parses as canonical +json carrying the reserved members with aeeRunBinding equal to the derived binding; method cap; batchRoot) are a HARD validity requirement: 'the following MUST hold or the attestation is invalid' (L286-289). Kind-constraint violations (a bad armedAt, posture/method mismatch, sealed conditions, run-chaining syntax, unknown aeeKind) make the record 'cover nothing' (L651-654, L672-674), invalidating only when the row is left without its required class cover. Both altitudes are quoted verbatim in the spec.

decisions.title: Method cap over covering records; unknown-kind and non-covering records excluded
decisions.reading: 'The row's method is no stronger than the weakest aeeMethod across its covering records' (L305-306) is computed over the referenced records that class-match and pass their kind constraints. A record whose aeeKind the consumer does not recognize 'covers nothing and is otherwise ignored' (L758-759), so it is excluded from the cap; likewise non-covering records. bad-304 locks the min-composition over covering records; ok-035 locks that a referenced unknown-kind record signed reconstructed neither invalidates an intercepted row nor lowers its cap.

decisions.title: Duplicate records by leaf hash
decisions.reading: 'Two byte-identical entries in observationRecords make the attestation invalid: a record's canonical identity is its leaf hash' (L800-802). The leaf hash is H(0x00 || DSSE PAE(payloadType, payload)), so a shared leaf hash and byte-identical PAE bytes are equivalent: a discriminating vector (distinct payloads, same leaf) is unconstructible, so bad-405 fully locks the reading.

decisions.title: Fail-closed vs malformed row members
decisions.reading: Members the recompute reads (containmentObserved, basis, method) are fail-closed on absence or unknown token (L487-490); on a substrate row a fail-closed label or method cannot satisfy class-match and makes the attestation invalid (L320-323). A present member of the wrong JSON type is a decode-layer fault making the statement malformed (a distinct altitude from an absent one), pinned for actualLayer by bad-506.

decisions.title: Clean-row actualLayer 'none' on every basis
decisions.reading: 'On a row whose containmentObserved label is from the carried labels but not in the caught set (a clean row), the producer MUST emit the literal string none' (L618-620). The text says 'a row', with no basis qualifier, so the rule binds artifact clean rows too. bad-503 locks the substrate twin; bad-818 locks the artifact clean row.

decisions.title: Coverage completeness at class + attack granularity; assessed classes are real manifest classes
decisions.reading: Coverage is an exhaustive, disjoint partition of the manifest's classes across assessedClasses / outOfScope / routedElsewhere (L372-379), each a real manifest class (an assessed class the manifest never carried is rejected); coverage integrity is exact set equality between row attackIds and the manifest's attacks for the assessed classes (L413-416). bad-816 locks a dropped class; bad-819 locks the mirror (a fabricated class padding assessedClasses); bad-806/807 lock the attack granularity.

decisions.title: Binding-version detection: derived mismatch and explicit read-first declaration
decisions.reading: A verifier has exactly one binding construction and rejects, fail-closed, a version it does not implement rather than attempt a second (L131-135); a construction it does not implement surfaces as aeeRunBinding failing to equal the v1 derivation (bad-303). An arming payload MAY carry an explicit aeeBindingVersion, read before deriving; a value the verifier does not implement makes the arming record cover nothing, distinguishably from a run-binding digest mismatch (L138-145, bad-726).

decisions.title: armedAt is RFC 3339 (UTC), compared to issuedAt as instants; issuedAt a valid RFC 3339 timestamp
decisions.reading: An arming record's armedAt is RFC 3339 UTC no later than issuedAt (L659-663); issuedAt is a required RFC 3339 timestamp (L827-829). Both rails parse and compare armedAt/issuedAt as instants. bad-701 (absent armedAt), bad-702 (armedAt after issuedAt), bad-810 (absent issuedAt), bad-811 (issuedAt not RFC 3339) lock the enforced behavior. A zero UTC offset is required: bad-727 locks a non-zero offset (+05:00), a valid instant but not UTC, as arming-covers-nothing.
decisions.underEnforcedSubReading: The zero-OFFSET strictness of 'RFC 3339 UTC' is not separately locked: both rails accept a non-Z offset (Go time.Parse and Python RFC3339_RE both admit [+-]HH:MM) and compare instants, so an offset armedAt whose instant precedes issuedAt is currently accepted. Locking zero-offset would change rail behavior on an arguably-ambiguous reading, so it is flagged in docs/interpretation-decisions-open.md rather than pinned by a vector.

decisions.title: Strict, canonical base64 for record payloads
decisions.reading: A covering record payload must decode as canonical +json valid I-JSON (L641-651). A payload re-encoded as non-canonical base64 (nonzero trailing bits) does not strict-decode and covers nothing: Go decodes with base64.StdEncoding.Strict() and the Python rail re-encode-compares, so both reject where a lenient decoder would accept.

decisions.title: Evidence tier per row over covering records; DSSE any-signature-verifies; keyid never the check
decisions.reading: The per-row evidence tier (attested/unattested/declared) is derived over the row's covering records; a record verifies when any of its signatures verifies (DSSE semantics) against a consumer-pinned substrate observation key, and keyid is 'an unauthenticated lookup hint and never the check itself' (L863-865). The tier is trust-relative (stage two), so a signature outcome is never a validity reject code; the readings are locked by ACCEPT vectors with pinned per-row tier expectations (ok-024) rather than reject vectors.

decisions.title: Whole statement parsed as strict I-JSON
decisions.reading: The whole statement JSON is parsed as strict I-JSON: a duplicate member anywhere in the statement, at any depth and not only inside a covering record payload, makes the statement malformed (L69-77). bad-725 carries raw statement bytes with a duplicate top-level member; the dict form cannot express a repeat, so a lenient last-wins parser would accept it.

decisions.title: Subject cardinality is unconditional (one subject on a statement of any basis)
decisions.reading: subject MUST contain exactly one entry on a statement of ANY basis (L122-126); a statement carrying zero or more than one subject is malformed regardless of whether any row is basis:substrate. Only the six binding-digest-input requirement (each carries a lowercase-64-hex sha256) stays scoped to substrate-row-carrying statements. Resolves open corner C (was permitted: the cardinality rule had been enforced only for substrate-carrying statements while its consequence sentence was substrate-scoped, so an artifact-only two-subject statement was wrongly accepted by all rails). bad-607 keeps a substrate row; bad-728 locks the artifact-only case.

decisions.title: Duplicate attackId rows are malformed (one row per executed attack)
decisions.reading: No two attackResults rows may carry the same attackId: 'one row per executed attack' (L385) is a well-formedness invariant, and a statement with a duplicate attackId across rows is malformed. Resolves open corner A (was permitted: coverage integrity set-compares row attackIds against the manifest, so a duplicate silently collapsed under set semantics and all rails accepted it). Both rails now detect the duplicate before building the rowID set. bad-729 locks it.

decisions.title: Coverage sets are a disjoint partition (assessedClasses / outOfScope / routedElsewhere)
decisions.reading: The three coverage sets are a disjoint partition of the manifest's classes: a class appears in exactly one of assessedClasses, outOfScope, routedElsewhere (a move, not a copy). A class in more than one of the three is malformed - a class both assessed and disclosed as a gap is contradictory. Resolves open corner B, a LIVE divergence: our two rails already reject overlap (disjoint partition) while the independent from-spec checker accepts it (completeness-only); no vector exercised it, so 134/134 parity was intact. Keeping the reject reading is the converged debate's recommended DIRECTION and is the one editorial call here, reversible at vetting. bad-730 locks it.
